import { build } from 'esbuild';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';
const file = process.argv[2] ?? 'src/module.ts';
const r = await build({ entryPoints: [file], bundle: true, minify: true, treeShaking: true,
  format: 'esm', platform: 'browser', target: 'es2022', write: false, metafile: true, logLevel: 'silent' });
const own = Object.entries(Object.values(r.metafile.outputs)[0].inputs)
  .filter(([path]) => !path.includes('node_modules/'))
  .reduce((sum, [, info]) => sum + info.bytesInOutput, 0);
console.log(file, gzipSync(r.outputFiles[0].contents, { level: 9 }).byteLength, 'bytes (min+gzip),', own, 'bytes of own code');

content.text:
I migrated the file and wrote it to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks with `tsc --strict`, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 1738 bytes (min+gzip), with 91 bytes of my own code.

I couldn't compare against the original. Lodash isn't installed, so `src/module.ts` doesn't build, and I didn't run the original or any equivalence test. I did check the es-toolkit functions by hand on tricky inputs, and I judged the lodash results from what I know of its behaviour.

- **`toSlug`** uses `kebabCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The non-compat `kebabCase` differs from lodash on ordinals: it gives `1-st-place` where lodash gives `1st-place`. The compat one gave `1st-place` and `4th-11th`. For `3rd2nd` it gave `3-rd-2nd`, which I believe matches lodash but couldn't confirm.
- **`byNameKey`** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit/array`. The non-compat version takes a function rather than a property string, so the adapter is `(row) => row.name`. Duplicate names keep the last row, as before.
- **`parseAmount`** uses `toNumber` from `es-toolkit/compat`. On the tricky cases I tried, it matched what lodash returns: `"0x1f"` gives 31, `" 12 "` gives 12, and `"9x80"` gives NaN.

The exported function signatures, `Row` and `Config` are unchanged, and no lodash import remains. Importing everything from `es-toolkit/compat` came to 4636 bytes, so I kept `keyBy` on the non-compat path.
